title: Sparks / TensorFold performance
description: Native TensorFold application-performance evaluation for one TP=2 GLM-5.3-Flash service. Temporary workstation collection, existing VictoriaMetrics storage.

options.content:
**TensorFold · CUDA · GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3 · TP=2 · spark-1 + spark-2**

One serving deployment, scraped at the leader every 5 seconds. **Evaluation collector runs on the workstation** and stops collecting when it sleeps or its Kubernetes tunnel closes. Runtime/model revisions remain unverified. See the [monitoring runbook](https://github.com/kelchm/home-lab/blob/main/sparks/monitoring/README.md) for semantics and limitations.

panels.title: Metrics reachable
panels.description: Fresh successful /metrics scrape; this does not prove the model can serve a request. Unavailable includes a stopped collector, stale ingestion, or failed target. Requires a sample younger than 20s.

panels.title: Live output · tokens/s
panels.description: Aggregate generated output across all streams, including replies in progress, over the latest 5-second scrape interval. Includes idle time; neither per-request decode speed nor SSE chunk rate. Supplied natively by this TensorFold build.

panels.title: Running requests
panels.description: Current requests in prefill or decode. This counts requests, not TP ranks.

panels.title: Waiting requests
panels.description: Native queued/held requests. Does not expose queue-wait duration or failed requests.

panels.title: Shared cache pool used
panels.description: Allocated shared pool rows minus free rows, divided by pool capacity. Includes retained prompt states. This is not GPU/host-memory usage or per-stream context occupancy.

panels.title: Output throughput
panels.description: Live output includes active replies. Finished-request output books the entire reply at completion, so it can spike after a long request. Both are aggregate rates over 1 minute.

panels.title: Time to first token · completed requests
panels.description: Server arrival to first generated token, recorded after the request finishes. Not client-visible TTFT. 5-minute window; quantiles require 20 samples and no >300s observations. Histogram buckets are coarse.

panels.title: Completed requests · last 5 minutes
panels.description: Counts finished latency observations in the window. Zero means no finished observations while the scrape is healthy; missing means unavailable. Fractional values can occur through counter extrapolation.

panels.title: Concurrency and stream states
panels.description: Native stream states supplied by the concurrent engine. Filling is multi-prefill activity; it is not a count of HTTP requests. Limit is the current stream ceiling.

panels.title: Prompt reuse · completed work
panels.description: Cached prompt tokens / prompt tokens across finished requests in a 5-minute window. Full prompt throughput includes cached input; uncached input estimates newly processed tokens. No data without finished prompt accounting.

panels.title: Prompt throughput · completed work
panels.description: Prompt tokens book at request completion, not while prefill is running. Uncached input = prompt minus cached prompt tokens; neither is a live prefill-speed measurement.

panels.title: Speculative acceptance · completed work
panels.description: Accepted / drafted tokens over finished requests in 5 minutes. No value when no drafts were verified. The mtp metric prefix does not establish which speculative drafter or MTP policy is active.

panels.title: Shared cache pool · tokens
panels.description: Pool capacity, occupied rows and free rows; includes kept prompt states. Distinct from tensorfold:kv_cache_usage_ratio, which uses a stream context window as its denominator.

panels.title: Retained prompts and context ceiling
panels.description: Kept prompt states may occupy the pool while idle. The effective context ceiling is per request, not currently used tokens.

panels.title: Context ceiling
panels.description: Effective per-request context ceiling reported by the running engine.

panels.title: Scrape duration
panels.description: Target scrape wall time. Timeout is 3s; interval 5s. No inference request is made by this collector.

panels.title: What this first pass can tell us

options.content:
Use this view to correlate **throughput, latency, concurrency, prompt reuse and pool pressure** during normal TensorFold use. Rates account for counter resets; ongoing requests contribute only to the live-output counter.

**Still unmeasured:** per-request decode speed / inter-token latency, client-visible TTFT, queue-wait duration, generation-stall detection, reliable error/cancellation counts, and node hardware / TP fabric health. A successful scrape is not an inference health check. Latency percentiles describe a mixed workload and are approximate; inspect sample counts before comparing runs.
